title: Audio Volume applet cause excessive CPU usage when visible, especially when on the Desktop
line: The Audio Volume widget on the desktop no longer records every audio device while a window covers it.
explanation: Each volume slider runs a level meter (a PulseAudio record stream per device) whenever the slider is visible. In the tray that stops when the popup closes, but a widget on the desktop is always visible as far as Qt knows, so it kept recording every device and using CPU even when a window hid it completely. The applet now watches the windows on its screen, desktop and activity (the same TasksModel query the panel uses for its opacity) and pauses its meters while a single non-minimized window covers the whole widget; Show Desktop, minimizing or moving the window brings them back.

commits.message:
applet: stop volume meters while a window covers the desktop widget

A widget on the desktop is always visible as far as Qt knows, so its
level meters kept recording every device even when a window hid it. Now
they pause while a window covers the whole widget, like in the tray.

BUG: 441555

media.caption: Master: the desktop widget sits under a maximized window while a sound plays; plasmashell keeps two PlasmaPA-VolumeMeter record streams open and uses 9 CPU ticks in 10 s
With the fix, same setup: no meter streams while the widget is covered, 1 CPU tick in 10 s

review.text: The cause is real (a desktop widget is always 'visible'), but the fix computes window occlusion inside the Audio Volume applet with its own TasksModel, which is the workaround Nicolas Fella warned about: every applet that wants to pause when hidden would have to copy it. It also only re-checks on the applet item's own x/y/size, which don't change when the widget is moved inside the desktop containment, and misses coverage by several windows together.
changes: Move the occlusion detection out of plasma-pa into libplasma (e.g. a Plasmoid/containment 'obscured' property, ideally fed by KWin's real occlusion knowledge) or at least the desktop containment, and have VolumeSlider only read that property.
Track the applet's position in screen coordinates (containment/applet container moves), not just the PlasmoidItem's x/y.
